blocks.x: Health payers sit between clinical reality and administrative machinery: prior authorization, coding integrity, quality programs and member experience all hinge on reading clinical evidence quickly and acting on it consistently — at HIPAA-grade privacy.

The workflows we industrialize here: Prior authorization, Claims coding integrity, Quality/HEDIS reporting, Member service resolution, Appeals and grievances. Each arrives with its current cycle times measured in the Diagnose phase, and each leaves the program governed by outcome SLOs rather than anecdotes.

items: Requests bounce for missing clinical evidence that exists in notes; turn-around times breach SLAs and clinicians revolt.
Claims codes and clinical narratives never reconcile; coding integrity and HEDIS-style quality reporting both suffer.
Coverage decisions cite policies inconsistently; member appeals overturn on documentation that was never surfaced.
Payer PHI is premium breach inventory; third-party partners extend the surface.
Benefit questions span plans, networks and formularies; agents guess and complaints escalate.
Core claims systems bend slowly; benefit design changes take quarters.

blocks.x: How we help — five priority capabilities

items: policy criteria mapped to chart evidence; submissions and appeals assembled — turnaround down 50-70%
codes + narratives unified for coding integrity and quality reporting — audit evidence complete
coverage logic citing medical policy passages with provenance — appeals overturn rate down
classification-aware DLP, access analytics and BAA governance — breach surface shrinking
strangler waves with parallel-run equivalence — benefit change lead time halved

blocks.x: A typical program here starts with a two-week diagnostic that measures the workflows named above and locks the baseline, moves through a gated proof on your data, then industrializes on platform rails with the sector's compliance evidence generated in-flight.
